solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Daughter wants nasty person? Blow!

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: Someone's daughter takes up with a rotter, and a parent mutters in dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance, interchangeable as expletives.

clue.text: Instrument Spike brought into group

indicators.note: something brought into a group is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a set is a group of things
a pin is a thin spike

explanation.surface: Someone called Spike joins a band on some instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: A little medicine provided by doctor before operation?

indicators.note: doctor comes before operation, so its letters lead

explanation.surface: A dose of medicine is given by a surgeon ahead of surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a tiny quantity of liquid medicine, as with eye drops.

clue.text: Something shocking that could be found in attics

indicators.note: suggests the letters of attics can be rearranged to yield something found in them

explanation.surface: A shocking discovery might be made up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' suggests scandal, but it refers to static electricity giving a small shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Static electricity gives a little electric shock when discharged.

clue.text: Abridge legal document

definitions.meaning: to shorten or condense, as a verb
a binding written agreement between parties

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to shorten; as a noun it is a binding agreement.

clue.text: One dervish dancing in a part of England

indicators.note: dancing shows the letters of one dervish are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A whirling dervish performs somewhere in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVONSHIRE is the older name for Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Devonshire is a county, so a region of England.

clue.text: Someone with an offer for model

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
a poser is one who poses, as a model does

explanation.surface: A person with an offer for a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposer puts forward an offer or motion, such as a marriage proposal.

clue.text: Ship beginning to sail with crew having little hesitation

indicators.note: the beginning to the word sail is just its first letter

parts.note: a team is a crew working together
er is the little sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A ship sets sail as the crew hesitates briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steam-powered ship.

clue.text: Piece of cloth covering end of power tool

indicators.note: one piece covering another wraps round it, so the other goes inside

parts.note: a towel is a piece of cloth for drying

indicators.note: end of the word power is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cloth is thrown over the end of a power tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for gardening or plastering.

clue.text: Position of a new church at end of street

indicators.note: the a-new-church pieces come at the end of the street piece, so street leads

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Where a newly built church stands at the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position, whether of the body or an opinion.

clue.text: Drink — a magical one ensnaring volunteers

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a magical drink is a potion
TA is the Territorial Army, British volunteer reservists

explanation.surface: A magic drink traps a group of volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is a drink, especially an alcoholic one.

clue.text: Artistic man — he and I may be troubled by people good at sums

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbance, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist and two others are bothered by number-crunchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmeticians are experts in arithmetic, so skilled at sums.

clue.text: Neglected male animal's needing comb

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep; the possessive gives RAMS
a hackle is a steel comb used to dress flax

explanation.surface: A ram, unkempt, needs its fleece combed.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackle is a little-known word for a flax comb, not the bird's neck feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle means badly kept and falling apart, as a neglected building is.

clue.text: Dance requiring zest, nothing additional

parts.note: tang is a sharp, zesty flavour
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dance needs energy and nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Book from this writer backed by arts graduate

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A book written by an author, supported by a graduate in the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the novel by Jane Austen, a book title.

clue.text: Publicise girl gaining a little weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Make it public that a girl has put on a little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make something known publicly.

clue.text: Agricultural establishment managed by companion

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A farm run by a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm for raising livestock.

clue.text: Henry longed to be married?

parts.note: H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance
itched means longed or yearned

explanation.surface: A man named Henry was eager to get wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is an informal idiom for getting married.

clue.text: Pleasure excursion? It's almost complete rubbish!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: tripe is slang for nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A complaint that a jolly outing was a waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey for pleasure.

clue.text: Healthy men nose around riverside town

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Fit men sniff around a town on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: HENLEY-ON-THAMES is an Oxfordshire town on the Thames, famous for its rowing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Henley stands on the banks of the Thames, so it is a town by a river.

clue.text: Pass by, please, after an accident

indicators.note: an accident leaves things mangled, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A plea to move on following a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by.

clue.text: A tonic can change behaviour

indicators.note: change indicates the letters of a tonic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tonic may alter one's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is something one does, part of one's behaviour or conduct.

clue.text: Copper to huff and puff following old Conservative resident

indicators.note: following means the copper-and-puff pieces come after the old Conservative pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to pant is to huff and puff for breath

explanation.surface: A policeman puffs along behind an old Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is someone living in a place, a resident.

clue.text: Little man with little energy is the enemy

parts.note: Tim is a short form of a man's name, Timothy
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A small man with little energy is the foe.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is the enemy is a familiar saying about time running out.

clue.text: Canine with tongue hanging out for food?

definitions.meaning: a dog panting because it feels the heat
a sausage served in a bun

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is an overheated dog; as a phrase it is a frankfurter in a roll.

clue.text: Get rid of some vicious thug

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Get rid of a few brutal hoodlums.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to expel or drive out, to get rid of.

clue.text: On board ship be without trousers

indicators.note: on board ship means placed inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
to lack is to be without

explanation.surface: Aboard ship someone goes without their trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are casual trousers.

clue.text: Drunk had somehow bumped into rodent in unruly residence

indicators.note: something that bumped into another has got inside it

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

indicators.note: drunk suggests a reeling state, so the letters of had are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk stumbles into a mouse in a chaotic house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' merely reinforces the anagram signal of 'Drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A madhouse is a place of chaos and uproar.
